title: Make the reply check cheaper

short.lead: The one cost that repeats most is a 5.5 second model call after every reply; pick how to cut it so I can build it.
short.hint: Tap a step to see it.
items: After every reply, a hook starts a second Claude (Haiku) to judge whether the reply claims something is impossible without proof. It runs even when no suspicious word is in the reply.
Nothing is built yet; this page only chooses how to cut the cost.

changes: Same check, runs only when it can matter
Measured here: with the model call 5,519 ms, with it off 63 ms. Every other hook costs about 70 ms. It is one call per reply, so it dominates a session.
Today: the judge runs after every reply that has a transcript and no flagged phrase (core.py _judge_check), a paid Haiku call.
Option A would run it only when a wider word list says a claim may be present.
You would wait about 5 seconds less after most replies and spend far fewer model calls.
choices: How should the reply check get cheaper?
Only run it when a wider word list flags the reply
Most replies have no claim, so most skip the 5.5 s call; a claim phrased in a way the list misses would go unchecked.
Run it in the background and show the verdict next turn
No waiting at all, but it can no longer block a bad reply, only warn after it.
Keeps full coverage; the 5.5 s stays on every reply.
A removes the wait on nearly every reply and keeps the blocking power for the replies that matter.

wrapup.summary: Cut the 5.5 second reply check that runs after every reply.
